title: Distributed File Storage (Google Drive)
intro: Design a scalable cloud file storage and synchronization service (Google Drive, Dropbox) supporting multi-gigabyte uploads, chunk deduplication, and cross-device sync.
objectives: Implement block-level chunking (4MB blocks) with content-addressed SHA-256 deduplication.
Separate relational file metadata (folder hierarchy, permissions) from immutable block object storage (S3).
Enable resumable uploads and delta sync for modified documents.
body:
### Architectural Decomposition
1. **Block Storage Service**: Large files are split on the client into uniform 4MB chunks. Each chunk is hashed using SHA-256 (`chunk_hash = SHA256(data)`). If the chunk hash already exists in storage, upload is skipped (**deduplication**).
2. **Metadata Database**: Stores file names, user directory hierarchies, version histories, and the ordered list of chunk hashes comprising each file.
3. **Sync Notification Service**: Long-polling or WebSocket connections notify other client devices when files change, instructing them to download only the modified 4MB delta chunks.
keyIdea: Separate metadata from blob data. Split files into content-addressed chunks to achieve bandwidth-saving deduplication and resumable multi-part uploads.

concepts.title: Content-Addressed Storage
concepts.body: Storing and naming chunks by their cryptographic SHA-256 hash ensures that identical files uploaded by different users share the same underlying storage.

concepts.title: Resumable Uploads
concepts.body: Client uploads chunks independently; if network drops at 90%, only the failed 4MB chunk needs retransmission, not the entire multi-gigabyte file.

examples: Dropbox infrastructure scaling block storage over Amazon S3 and custom Magic Pocket clusters.

quiz.prompt: What is the primary benefit of splitting large files into 4MB chunks named by their SHA-256 hash?
options: Enables global deduplication, delta sync, and resilient resumable uploads
Prevents files from being downloaded over mobile networks
quiz.explanation: Content-addressed chunking enables bandwidth-saving deduplication and allows uploading only modified chunks.
